subject: Critical: Reserved GPU throughput shortfall impacting ClearBridge checkout flows
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@clearbridge.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: platform-support@clearbridge.com
Date: 2026-09-04T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production: checkout error spike + tail latency (reserved capacity mismatch)

Hannah / David —

We're seeing a significant increase in checkout latency and ~3% 5xx rate across our production fleet starting ~07:45 PDT. This is affecting ~12% of checkouts and causing real business impact. Per our contract we have a reserved throughput profile (200 qps sustained) but the telemetry indicates token throughput is far below that during peak—requests are queueing and timing out.

I attached a short log excerpt (clearbridge_latency_sample_0903.log) and a snapshot I pulled from your metrics UI. Can you confirm whether our reserved pool is being throttled or if this is noisy neighbor behavior? We need either immediate mitigation or a short-term burst allocation while you investigate.

We appreciate a clear ETA and whether Redwood will credit ClearBridge for degraded service.

Sanjay
Platform Ops — ClearBridge

Attachments: clearbridge_latency_sample_0903.log (text), reserved_throughput_snapshot_0904.pdf (pdf)

Team — looping you in. Customer ClearBridge is reporting a reserved throughput shortfall (200 qps committed) with increased latency and 5xxs. High business impact.

Immediate asks:
- David: can you validate whether the reserved pool for ClearBridge is healthy / whether eviction or noisy neighbor is causing headroom loss?
- Irene: can you pull the most recent reservation allocations and physical GPU assignment for their account?
- Marissa: be prepared to propose a mitigation plan / customer comms and evaluate credits.

Customer is requesting a burst allocation if we can provide one while we fix the underlying issue. Please update this thread with concrete next steps and ETA.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt | Account Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: checkout error spike + tail latency (reserved capacity mismatch)

Hannah — quick update after an initial triage:

Observations:
- The ClearBridge reserved pool shows sustained CPU/GPU utilization at ~98% on a subset of nodes.
- We observed KV cache fragmentation on the host group assigned to their reservation which is increasing per-request latency.
- One tenant (internal id tenant-179) has a sudden surge in long-context requests that are consuming batch headroom and causing lower effective QPS for ClearBridge despite the reservation being "present" at the orchestration layer. This looks like noisy-neighbor behavior within the dedicated pool.

Immediate mitigations I can execute (ETA 30m - 2h depending on approvals):
1) Evict the offending tenant 179 workloads from the ClearBridge node set and re-route them to pre-emption tier (temporary).  (Impact: 5-10 min disruption for that tenant, immediate headroom recovery for ClearBridge.)
2) Apply conservative batching caps and reduce max sequence length routing for ClearBridge to lower per-request token cost (limits throughput loss, low risk to prompt outputs).
3) Temporarily grant a burst overlay (+40% QPS) by assigning two additional GPU hosts to their reservation pool from the burst-capacity pool. Requires Ops lead approval and coordination with capacity controller.

I'll start step 2 now and run a deeper trace on KV cache eviction patterns. If we need burst overlay I need green light from leadership to allocate.

Logs: see attached quick trace in the drive link (JIRA-OPS-9921).

—David
Senior SRE, Runtime Operations
Redwood Inference

Sanjay — thanks for flagging and for the logs. We're treating this as an urgent priority. Below is a short, actionable mutual action plan so you know what to expect:

1) Next 30m: SRE (David) will apply conservative batching caps for ClearBridge traffic and limit long-context routings. Expect partial latency improvement within ~15-30 minutes.
2) Next 60-120m: Eviction of noisy tenant and node rebalancing if the trace confirms sustained interference.
3) 2-6 hours: If headroom remains insufficient, we will apply a temporary burst overlay (+40% QPS) to your reservation for up to 24 hours.
4) 24-72 hours: Post-incident root-cause analysis and permanent remediation plan (kernel tuning and stronger tenant isolation).

We propose a one-time service credit covering the period of visible degradation; I will confirm the exact amount with finance after the incident window. Attached is a draft mutual_action_plan (mutual_action_plan_clearbridge_20260904.docx).

We're also opening a prioritized Jira (JIRA-OPS-9921) and will send live updates there. Hannah will lead customer comms.

—Marissa
